propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing stale-lock detection to incorrectly judge a dead process with a recycled pid number as alive, creating an unbounded lock wedge

When current_start is None and only a live-pid number verdict exists, the lock must be bounded by _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S instead of exempted, since the verdict is unqualified by actual process start-time evidence

A genuinely live lock holder cannot reach the stale-check code because it holds the exclusive fcntl leg for the entire mkdir-leg lifetime; any arrival at the ceiling check is evidence the stamped owner released, so the ceiling only fires on orphans

The owner-identity and staleness cluster is extracted from lock.py to lock_owner.py to satisfy the 800-line module-size limit while preserving one-way dependency and avoiding re-export shims that would silently break monkeypatch tests
